keepFraction.description: A shift is kept when this share of the real samples stays usable (default 0.9)

seed.description: Seed of the null's random stream (default 20261020); recorded in the result

snrColumn.description: Map vs catalog only: the declared value column holding P, for the optional filter P/σP ≥ snrMin; off unless both columns are named

snrSigmaColumn.description: Map vs catalog only: the declared value column holding σP

snrMin.description: The filter's k (default 3, the threshold the owner's comparison script uses); rows with P/σP below it are excluded and counted, rows with P or σP missing are excluded with their own reason

strataBins.description: With stratifyId: the number of equal-count bins of the third map (default 5); not with strataEdges. Tied values are never split, so a heavy tie gives fewer bins

strataEdges.description: With stratifyId: user-set bin edges in the third map's unit, strictly increasing; a bin is [lower, upper) and the last one is closed; pixels outside them are left out and counted

datasetId.description: A map declared as an axial orientation map, with its frame and quantity

otherId.description: A point catalog with a declared angle, or a second declared orientation map on the same grid

masks.description: Masks of the first map, each with its own policy (ADR 0055); refused for a comparison with a catalog

stratifyId.description: Map against map only: a scalar map on the same grid (a column density, a signal-to-noise map). The comparison is repeated inside bins of it and the result carries `stratified`. It needs a brightness unit (BUNIT or declared) and is refused when it is declared as an orientation map, lives on a host or does not share the grid. The comparison without it is unchanged

RelativeOrientationSummary.description: Every number with its definition, the parameters as used (defaults filled in, seed included), counts and exclusions (ADR 0047).

map.description: The map's declaration as used (unit, frame, quantity, rotation to B, celestial frame, reliability), its size nx, ny and pixel scale, and the compass (see Compass) at the map centre

other.description: The second map's declaration as used (map vs map)

catalog.description: The catalog's frame, angle quantity, rotation to B, row count and uncertainty column (map vs catalog)

snr_filter.description: The P/σP filter as applied (columns, k, rule, rows excluded below k and for missing values); null when it was off

stratified.description: Map against map with stratifyId: the comparison's statistics inside bins of a third map (ADR 0047, amendment)

third_map.description: The third map's unit and whose it is: its BUNIT, or declared or corrected by the author

third_map_missing.description: Of those, pixels with no value in the third map

outside_edges.description: Of the rest, pixels outside user-set edges

lo.description: Lower edge, in the third map's unit

hi.description: Upper edge, in the third map's unit (included for the last bin)

centre.description: Middle of the edges, in the third map's unit

median.description: Median of the third map over the bin's pixels

am.description: AM = mean of cos 2Δψ over the bin; null for an empty bin, never 0

bootstrap_am_16_84.description: 16th and 84th percentiles of AM over resamples of the bin's pixels (assumes independent pixels, so optimistic)

bootstrap_samples.description: Resamples used; fewer for a large bin

prs.description: Projected Rayleigh statistic of the bin (no p-value: pixels are correlated)

independent_beams.description: Approximate number of independent beams in the bin; null when a map declares no beam

am.description: AM expected for independent uniform angles: 0

uniform_reference.description: The statistic's value and spread for uniform angles, for the bin's pixel and beam counts

LevelsSigma.description: Levels at multiples of a robust noise estimate of the contoured channel: sigma = 1.4826 x MAD of its finite pixels (astropy.stats.mad_std). It is the scatter of the whole plane, signal included, and is labelled as such.

sigma.description: The sigma the levels were drawn with, recorded by a figure. A recomputed sigma that differs is refused (the data changed).

OverlayGeometryRequest.description: Geometry of one overlay on the base dataset named in the path.

spacing.description: For orientation with auto sampling: the wanted distance between lines, in base pixels (the pane's gapPx divided by its scale). Ignored otherwise.

OverlayGeometryHeader.description: The JSON header of an overlay geometry frame. Every position is in base pixels: 0-based, pixel centres at integers, y up (FITS order). Extra keys may be present and are not part of the contract.

paths.description: contours, beam, grid: the payload starts with paths pairs (group, vertex count) and continues with the vertices as (x, y) pairs. group is the level index (contours), 0 for the beam, 0 for a line of constant longitude and 1 for one of constant latitude (grid).

segments.description: orientation: the payload is segments quadruples (x, y, angle, weight): angle in degrees counter-clockwise from the base's +x pixel axis towards +y, weight in [0, 1] (1 without a reliability map).

placement.description: How the overlay was placed on the base.

levels.description: contours: the levels traced, in unit

simplified.description: Present when the vertices were over budget and simplified (Ramer-Douglas-Peucker) with this tolerance in base pixels.

step.description: orientation: the sampling step used, in overlay pixels

spacing_px.description: orientation: the distance between samples in base pixels

conversion.description: orientation, catalog with vectors: how the stored angles became B-field orientation in the base pixel frame

reliability.description: orientation: present when the declared reliability map was read (for length, opacity or a threshold)

markers.description: catalog: the payload is markers rows of six numbers (x, y, vector angle, vector length, colour value, row): x, y in base pixels; vector angle in degrees counter-clockwise from the base's +x pixel axis towards +y, in [0, 180), and vector length in base pixels (NaN: no vector at this row); the colour value as in the catalog (NaN: unknown); row is the 1-based row number in the table.

counts.description: catalog: every row of the table is in exactly one of no_position, outside, filtered and drawn.

filter.description: catalog: the row filter as applied, counted over the rows on the base.

vectors.description: catalog: the orientation vectors, when drawn.

color.description: catalog: the colour column and the range its legend states.

catalog.description: catalog: how the table was read.

skipped_lines.description: Lines of the file that were not rows (see the catalog's parse report).

nGauss.description: Gaussians per pixel, as the run's records declare; 0 when they do not

isCrop.description: the dataset is the crop the fit used

refusal.description: why the components cannot be drawn over this dataset

RohsaRunView.description: A ROHSA decomposition run whose components could be drawn over a dataset: the dataset is the run's crop or exactly on its grid. A cube with the crop's axis lengths but another (or unconfirmed) grid is listed with the reason it is refused.

index_bytes.description: size of the sidecar index: 8 bytes per pixel

where.description: Which machine builds and keeps the index: this one, or the host that holds the fit (ADR 0046). On a host the .dat is read there, the sidecar is written in the account's own cache folder there, and only this state and single pixels travel.

RohsaIndexState.description: Progress of the index of a ROHSA .dat. building: call again; ready: pixels can be read; refused: the file is not the ROHSA row layout, with the reason and example lines.

k.description: 1-based Gaussian number within the pixel, in file order

amp.description: fitted amplitude in the crop's brightness unit; 0 is a real value

mean_channel.description: 0-based channel index: the file's value minus 1

valid.description: false when sigma is not positive and finite; such a component is not drawn

centre.description: km/s on the crop's spectral axis; null without a resolved velocity axis

t_doppler_k.description: 121.1 K (km/s)^-2 x sigma^2: an upper limit on the kinetic temperature

conventions.description: the conventions applied, in words: columns, 1-based mean, sigma, model, invalid components, FWHM, T_D

RohsaComponentsHeader.description: The JSON header of a rohsa components frame.

SweepParam.description: One swept setting. A sweep varies one to three of them; the product of the list lengths is at most 64.

key.description: A config setting the VGT template can change (dn, ker, noise, ...)

label.description: How the owner's screen names it (for example the Greek letter); empty means the key

values.description: The explicit list, as typed; never reparsed. Letters, digits and . _ + - only

SweepRequest.description: A sweep to create or preview. Nothing is submitted by either.

name.description: Starts each job's name (letters, digits, . _ -, up to 32)

baseRunId.description: A run made by one of our jobs; its job is the base. Give baseJobId or baseRunId, not both

note.description: Why, kept with every draft (at most 500 characters)

Requested.description: What a script asks the scheduler for, read from its #SBATCH lines; zero means the script does not say

SweepTotals.description: The requested resources of the drafts. Each is the largest single request; the total is the sum

cpuSecondsAtLimit.description: Sum of CPUs x time limit: the most the requests could use

SweepEstimate.description: What the base job measured (ADR 0045). A guide, not a prediction: a changed parameter can change time and memory

SweepPreview.description: What creating the sweep would make; nothing is stored

held.description: A draft edited after the owner approved the sweep: it is not submitted

usage.description: What sacct reported when the job ended (the Job usage object); null before

Sweep.description: A grid of linked draft jobs and where it stands

state.description: What the owner authorised: draft nothing is submitted; running approved and being submitted; stopped cancelled or stopped on a failure; finished every submittable job has been submitted. Not whether the jobs succeeded

waitingOn.description: Jobs that hold a slot or are held, in words, so a stall is visible

pending.description: Drafts that will still be submitted

template.description: The base job's template: vgt or rohsa; empty when the base job is gone

kind.description: Why the line differs from the base; other is never expected

unexpected.description: Differing lines that are not a swept setting, the output folder or the job name

sizing.description: ROHSA only: what the owner's sizing table suggests for this draft's crop and Gaussian count, beside what it requests (every draft requests what the base job did)

SweepReview.description: The scripts of the drafts still to be submitted, how each differs from the base, and what they request

baseEditedLines.description: Lines (removed and added together) by which the base job's script differs from what its own settings render: the owner edited it by hand. Drafts are rendered from the settings and do not carry those edits; they are compared with the rendered text, so these lines never show as unexpected

sweepHash.description: Names the exact scripts shown; approval must quote it

template.description: The base job's template: vgt or rohsa

defaultConcurrency.description: The limit used when approval names none: 1, one job at a time

concurrencyNote.description: Why one at a time matters for this kind of sweep; empty when there is nothing specific to say (ROHSA: the shared, rebuilt source folder)

concurrency.description: At most this many of the sweep's jobs queued or running; 1 is sequential. Absent means 1; 0 is refused

stopOnFailure.description: Stop scheduling when a job fails; default false: a failure changes nothing for the others and nothing is retried

cancelRunning.description: Also ask Slurm to cancel the sweep's queued and running jobs

SweepMetric.description: A declared number of a run; value null is not recorded, never zero

unit.description: Empty when the runs declared different units

unitsDiffer.description: The runs declared different units: not one quantity, so not plotted

value.description: Null is a gap: no recorded value or no run yet, never zero

SweepPlot.description: A metric against one parameter, one line per combination of the other parameters

numeric.description: The x values are numbers on a numeric axis; otherwise categories in list order

SweepGrid.description: The grid as a table: one row per job in parameter order with what its run declared. No row is labelled best

SceneLine.description: A saved line: the path a position-velocity diagram is cut along (ADR 0049). Whole-pixel vertices (0-based, y from the bottom), a width across the path and its unit. A line has no area, so it is never the working region and no spectrum or histogram is taken of it.

ChannelGrid.description: A grid of channel-map panels of one dataset that share one colour scale (ADR 0049). A separate versioned description from scene/1: a scene is what one pane draws, a grid is many panels. A figure stores one or the other, told apart by `schema`. The shared scale is stored as numbers with where they came from, never recomputed per panel.

average.description: Channels each panel is the mean of (1: one channel); not more than the stride.

spectral.description: The unit the labels are in; absent means the file's own axis unit.

source.description: Where the limits came from, in words.

preview.description: The block-mean step the panels were drawn at (1: the full plane) and their size as drawn; every panel and all together are within the transfer caps.

render.description: What the composed picture said beyond the description, so "draw again" reproduces it. Absent from grids saved before.

overlaysNotDrawn.description: How many overlays of the map were visible but not drawn on the panels (the caption states it)

scaleSource.description: The whole sentence on where the shared limits came from, as the caption printed it; display.source keeps its first 190 characters

ChannelGridPlan.description: The plan of a channel-map grid: JSON only, no payload. Each panel is fetched by the plane route (one channel) or the slab route (a mean of several), at the preview step stated here.

mean.description: true for a panel that averages several channels

spectral.description: Spectral value of the panel's first and last channel in `spectral.unit`; null where undefined.

flagged.description: Channels of the panel the provider flagged; null when the file declares no flags.

scale.description: The one scale every panel shares. lo and hi are null only when the sampled panels hold no finite pixel.

spectral.description: How the spectral labels were made (ADR 0040). `refused` is set when the asked conversion could not be done: the native values and unit stay and the labels say so.

SlabHeader.description: The JSON header of a slab frame: a plane header plus what was averaged. NaN in the payload means no value, never zero.

PvRequest.description: A position-velocity slice along a path of whole-pixel vertices (0-based, y from the bottom), sampled at about one-pixel spacing with several samples across the width averaged.

interpolation.description: linear is bilinear interpolation (a sample with a non-finite neighbour is excluded); nearest takes the nearest pixel, no interpolation.

PvHeader.description: The JSON header of a position-velocity frame. Payload (little-endian): float64 offset[offsets], float64 axis[channels_returned] (NaN = undefined), float32 value[channels_returned][offsets] (NaN = no value), uint8 count[channels_returned][offsets] (finite samples averaged).

outside_samples.description: Samples that fell outside the image; they hold no value.

spectral.description: How the spectral labels were made (ADR 0040). `refused` is set when the asked conversion could not be done: the native values and unit stay and the labels say so.

sky.description: The file's sky facts (kind, frame and its status).

ValueStats.description: Statistics of the finite values of a computed map or diagram (a slab, a position-velocity slice). null when nothing is finite.

RohsaSizing.description: A resource request suggested for a ROHSA run by the table in the owner's hpc/irgetas/submit_rohsa.sh. It is a suggestion; nothing applies it

cropSize.description: The crop size used (0 is the whole cube)

assumed.description: Inputs not given, so the script's own default was used (crop_size 0, n_gauss 6)

scriptPartition.description: The partition that script submits to; a site setting shown for information and never applied

basis.description: Where the numbers come from, in words

TransferVerification.description: What was checked after the bytes arrived. status is empty until then. verified means the size and the SHA-256 (for a folder, rsync's content checksum, which is not SHA-256: see method) matched on both ends after the transfer; anything else is unverified, with the reason in note. A copy is never called verified on the strength of rsync finishing.

sourceSha256.description: Computed on the source's own machine after the transfer; empty when it could not be

Transfer.description: One entry of the transfer queue between this computer and a host (ADR 0051). sourcePath is read, destDir is the existing folder written into; direction says which is on the host.

kind.description: Empty until the source has been looked at (a download)

name.description: The wanted name at the destination

finalName.description: The name chosen when the first attempt started (it differs from name for keep_both); never changes afterwards

policy.description: What to do when the name exists at the destination. Only replace ever overwrites.

state.description: waiting is a retry after a lost connection (nextAttemptAt); conflict waits for the owner's decision. done says the bytes arrived, not that they are verified: see verification.

checksum.description: The next attempt compares contents instead of trusting size and time

fails.description: Attempts in a row that moved no data; the wait before the next one grows with it

warning.description: From the host's last storage look, for an upload that may not fit; empty when there is nothing to say

datasetId.description: The dataset a verified download was registered as

TransferRequest.description: Queue a transfer. A download reads a path inside the host's source roots into an existing folder inside this computer's source roots; an upload reads a file or folder inside this computer's source roots into an existing folder inside the host's source roots. Paths are absolute; a remote source may not contain * ? [ (rsync would expand them).

name.description: Name at the destination; the source's own name by default

policy.description: Default ask: an identical file counts as already there, a different one waits for a decision

discardPartial.description: Delete the unfinished file of a download. A partial file on a host is never deleted by Vesqira.

TransferRegistered.description: The dataset a verified download was registered as (201 the first time, 200 when it already was). Its derived record names the host and path as an external reference and the hash compared.

by.description: What computed it: "this computer" or "worker on <host name>", or "hashed while copying".

IdentityStamp.description: A computed value with when and by what it was computed.

hostId.description: 0 for a file on this computer, otherwise the host that holds it

primary.description: The file the dataset was registered from. Dataset.path and hostId are this location.

link.description: Why the location belongs to the dataset. registered: the primary, no claim. verified: equal full SHA-256 (the same bytes). probable: same size and equal sampled fingerprint, which is NOT proof. declared: the researcher's word, nothing was proven. stale: was verified or probable against an earlier version of the registered file, which has changed since; not read from until compared again.

sampledFingerprint.description: A SHA-256 over the file size, the primary FITS header and 16 blocks of 64 KiB at fixed offsets (algorithm sampled/1; see LocationList.sampledCovers). A different value proves the files differ; an equal value does not prove they are the same. null: not computed.

fullSha256.description: The SHA-256 of every byte. null: not computed.

DatasetLocation.description: One place a dataset's bytes are (ADR 0053).

checked.description: false: a file on a host, which is not contacted to answer this

ReadsFrom.description: Where the viewer would read the dataset from now: files on this computer before files on a host, the registered file before others, and only the registered file or a location verified to hold the same bytes.

unavailable.description: Present when nothing can be read; the reason.

hashing.description: Full-hash tasks by location id; a finished or cancelled task is simply gone.

sampledCovers.description: What a sampled fingerprint covers, in one sentence, for display.

declare.description: Say that the file is the same dataset when nothing computed can tell. Never overrides proof of a difference.

mode.description: sampled: computed now (about 1 MiB read). full: queued in the background, one at a time, capped and cancellable. cancel: stop a full hash.

LocationRefusal.description: A 409 that says why the file was not linked, or why registering it is offered as a location instead.

relation.description: verified: equal full SHA-256. probable: same size and sampled fingerprint, not proof.

reason.description: newer_file: a run's output folder gained a later file of the same role (a re-run writes psi_<stem>_1.fits instead of overwriting). changed_in_place: the registered file's size or time differs. figure_data_changed: the dataset behind a figure is not the bytes the figure was drawn from.

datasetId.description: The dataset the notice is about when it exists; 0 for a newer file that is not registered

differs.description: What differs. fingerprint is said only when both values were computed and differ.

NewerNotice.description: A notice only: nothing is swapped or redrawn.

role.description: source: the figure's dataset. overlay: a dataset an overlay was drawn from. reliability: a reliability map that set the opacity, length or threshold of orientation lines.

declarations.description: The declarations in force when the figure was saved (ADR 0042, section 5): the declared unit, the orientation interpretation and a hash of the catalog declaration, each with who declared it. An empty object records that none existed. Absent on figures saved before this was recorded.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the declaration's content (not of its time or staleness)

redrawnFrom.description: Set on a figure made by "draw again": the figure it redraws, which is never changed (ADR 0042, section 5). Owner API only.

FigureIdentity.description: What was known about the bytes of each dataset when the figure was saved. Owner API only, never part of the reviewer-safe provenance.

TerminalOpen.description: Ask for a terminal session (only with --enable-terminal, ADR 0029). The host is chosen by id, never by a free-form string.

tab.description: chosen by the page, one per browser tab; a new session for the same tab ends the previous one

hostId.description: a registered host to open ssh to; 0 or absent opens the user's login shell on this computer

TerminalSession.description: The one-time credential for the WebSocket at GET /api/terminal. Shown once; send it only as a WebSocket subprotocol.

protocol.description: the subprotocol the server selects: vesqira.terminal.v1

expiresInSeconds.description: how long the token can still be used to connect

idleSeconds.description: no input for this long ends the session

ControlsStated.description: Who is responsible for a block of controls: declared (a person said so, not checked here) or verified (Vesqira ran it and records what it ran).

ControlsSmoothing.description: The kernel applied before the result was made. A width always comes with its unit; width null means smoothing was applied and its width is not stated.

ControlsNoise.description: How the noise was described to the analysis.

estimated.description: How the noise was estimated, in words.

ControlsConstruction.description: How a control or null was built. Verified only for a null Vesqira ran itself (relative orientation).

Controls.description: Smoothing, noise model and control construction stated for a result. A block that is null was not stated, which is not the same as none applied.

ControlsDeclaration.description: What the researcher states. Replaces the stored statement: a block that is left out or null is cleared. Basis, author and time are set by the server (declared, researcher, now) whatever is sent.

unit.description: required with a width, refused without one

note.description: at most 300 characters; required for kind other

estimated.description: how the noise was estimated; at most 300 characters

params.description: lower-case names (letters, digits, _), each once; values at most 80 characters

EnvDifference.description: One fact compared between two runs, or between a parent run and the code folder as it is now. unknown means at least one side did not observe it; it is never reported as matched.

blocking.description: differed in a fact a strict rerun requires to be equal

why.description: for unknown: which side did not observe it

parent.description: null: the parent run did not have this setting

now.description: null: the draft does not have it

RerunCheck.description: What can be said about a rerun draft before it is submitted (ADR 0054). A strict draft with blocking true is refused by the submit route.

codeChecked.description: the host answered the read-only look at the code folder; adapted drafts do not ask

settingsKnown.description: false when the parent run's settings were not kept, so no change can be marked

SceneLink.description: The link group this pane was in when the scene was made (ADR 0042, section 4): how its panes followed each other. Panes belong to one group by id; the group's name is the person's.

name.description: Named by the person; printable text without line breaks

basis.description: same-grid: the server confirmed one pixel grid, so a pixel, a channel index and an image point mean the same in each pane. wcs: positions and channels are carried through the worker's WCS transformation (astropy), with the spectral part refused when the frames differ.

datasets.description: The datasets of the group's panes, this scene's own included

SceneLinkFacets.description: What the group links: the cursor (sky position), the channel (spectral world value) and the view (the sky region in view).

LinkRequest.description: What to compute for linking the dataset in the path (the first map) to another (the second). At least one of region, points and channels.

region.description: A window of this map in pixels: 0-based, pixel centres at integers, y up (FITS order). Widened to a half-pixel grid before it is used.

points.description: Pixels of the first map to map exactly (in the region's pixel convention); only with a region

channels.description: Also map every channel of the first map to the second map's nearest channel by spectral world value

LinkSky.description: How the first map's pixels land in the second's. Either refused (the reason) or an affine approximation over the region with its measured error, plus exact positions of the points asked for. Every number comes from astropy in the worker.

refused.description: Why the maps cannot be related on the sky (no celestial WCS, a frame that cannot be built, a region where the transform is undefined)

affine.description: [a, b, tx, c, d, ty]: x' = a x + b y + tx and y' = c x + d y + ty, in the maps' pixel convention

region.description: A window of this map in pixels: 0-based, pixel centres at integers, y up (FITS order). Widened to a half-pixel grid before it is used.

max_error_px.description: The worst distance in second-map pixels between the affine and the exact transform, measured on a grid other than the one it was fitted on, corners included

scale.description: Second-map pixels per first-map pixel (square root of the affine's determinant)

LinkSpectral.description: How the first map's channels land in the second's. Either refused (the reason: spectral frames differ or are not stated, a convention or rest frequency that does not allow it, no spectral axis) or one entry per channel of the first map.

unit.description: The first map's axis unit; residuals are in it

index.description: The second map's nearest channel for each channel of the first (null where the first map's value is not finite)

residual.description: Second map's channel value minus the first's, in the first map's axis unit

outside.description: True where the value lies beyond the second map's range by more than half a channel: that channel is not followed

LinkReply.description: The worker's reply, as it is: two independent parts, each null when not asked for.

ChannelLink.description: Whether the two maps' channels may be linked by index on one grid: the spectral reference frame (SPECSYS) must be declared by both and equal. Separate from grid compatibility, which guards sky position only.

compatible.description: Shape, axis types, units, reference values, steps, rotation and the celestial frame all match: pixels correspond one to one

vpnCommand.description: The VPN client's argv, stored and run exactly as written, without a shell, as the user. First element: an absolute path or a bare program name found in PATH; at most 16 parts of 512 bytes (2048 in all); no NUL or line breaks. Empty or absent means none.

vpnDisconnectCommand.description: Optional argv that disconnects the VPN; same rules.

Host.description: A remote machine reached with the user's own ssh.

vpnCommand.description: The VPN client's argv, stored and run exactly as written, without a shell, as the user. First element: an absolute path or a bare program name found in PATH; at most 16 parts of 512 bytes (2048 in all); no NUL or line breaks. Empty or absent means none.

vpnDisconnectCommand.description: Optional argv that disconnects the VPN; same rules.

reachable.description: what this session last learned (a host check, the job watcher or a VPN command); not stored, unknown until asked

reachableAt.description: when that was learned; absent while unknown

exitCode.description: once the client ended; -1 when ended by a signal

output.description: the end of what the client printed (at most 16 KiB, control sequences removed); never written to the audit log

vpnClient.description: The VPN client Vesqira started for this host in this session (in memory; a restart forgets it, the client keeps running). Absent when none was started.

HostListEntry.description: A host with what this session last learned about reaching it.

vpnCommand.description: The VPN client's argv, stored and run exactly as written, without a shell, as the user. First element: an absolute path or a bare program name found in PATH; at most 16 parts of 512 bytes (2048 in all); no NUL or line breaks. Empty or absent means none. Refused with 403 unless the server runs with --enable-vpn.

vpnDisconnectCommand.description: Optional argv that disconnects the VPN; same rules.

vpnCommand.description: The VPN client's argv, stored and run exactly as written, without a shell, as the user. First element: an absolute path or a bare program name found in PATH; at most 16 parts of 512 bytes (2048 in all); no NUL or line breaks. Empty or absent means none.

vpnDisconnectCommand.description: Optional argv that disconnects the VPN; same rules.

HostVpnConfig.description: Replaces both commands; leaving one out clears it.

HostVpnAction.description: The only thing the page may send: which stored command to run. Any other field is refused.

exitCode.description: the program's exit status; -1 when it did not start, is still running or was ended by a signal

timedOut.description: connect: the host did not become reachable within the wait (about two minutes); the client keeps running. disconnect: the command did not finish in time and was stopped with everything it started

output.description: stdout and stderr together (a client's log file, last 16 KiB), control sequences removed; why the program did not start when it did not. Never written to the audit log.

reachable.description: the result of the host reachability check run after the command

message.description: for example: VPN client started; the host became reachable after 12 s

policy.description: Stated for every mask: there is no default and no global policy. `weight` only where the analysis has weights (relative orientation); the policy for a no-value mask is exclude.

weight.description: With the weight policy: the factor a flagged pixel counts with

Mask.description: A typed mask (ADR 0055): a derived uint8 FITS file flagging pixels of a dataset for a stated reason. It changes nothing in the dataset and is applied only where an operation names it with a policy.

hostId.description: Where the mask file lives: 0 for this computer, otherwise the host whose derived folder holds it, next to the dataset's file (ADR 0064). Its bytes stay there.

type.description: missing: no value in the file (NaN, BLANK), computed and never declared. Zero is a value and is never `missing`.

channels.description: 0: one plane that applies to every channel; otherwise one plane per channel

tier.description: How far the interpretation is established (ADR 0055): verified (a check the app ran), declared (the researcher), inferred (a rule, named by declaredBy, with its mapping version) or unresolved. Not the worker's header statuses: "declared" there means the file says it.

mappingVersion.description: The version of the rule's mapping, for an inferred interpretation; empty for any other tier

method.description: computed: by the worker from the data and a stated rule. regions: from saved regions. import: from a file the researcher provided. carried: cut, resampled or smoothed with the data it describes by a cutout, slab, subset, align or convolve; its rule says which and from which mask

rule.description: How the mask was made, as the worker described it: the rule, the estimator, the threshold and where sigma or the threshold came from, the regions, or the file imported

sourceIdentity.description: What is recorded about the bytes the mask was made from: sha256:<hex>, sampled:<fingerprint> (not proof) or empty

stale.description: The dataset's size or modification time differs from when the mask was made: it is not applied until it is made again

sourceDataset.description: The registered file an imported mask was made from, when the row records it (masks made before the id was recorded do not)

method.description: missing: computed from the data (type missing). low_snr: value / sigma < k. saturated: value >= threshold. regions: user_excluded from saved regions. import: a registered image of the same grid, with its declared type and the meaning of nonzero

source.description: Where the saturation threshold comes from (required)

nonzero.description: What a nonzero pixel of the imported file means

FigureTier.description: How far one interpretation behind a figure is established (ADR 0055): the brightness unit, the orientation declaration, or a mask that was applied to the result. No id and no path.

rule.description: For an inferred interpretation: the rule that proposed it

SceneRender.description: How the base raster of a saved figure was drawn, so "draw again" reproduces it (ADR 0042, section 5). Only a stored figure has one; a live pane's scene and a figure saved before it existed have none, and draw again from their PNG only.

canvas.description: The canvas the plane was drawn on: a whole multiple of the plane when zoomed in, the display size when zoomed out. At most 2^26 pixels; a figure whose canvas is larger is stored without this record and is drawn from its PNG only.

nodata.description: The two colours of the hatching that marks a pixel with no value (never a colour of the scale), as the theme gave them

figureWidth.description: The width in pixels the figure was composed at

role.description: source: the figure's dataset. overlay: a dataset an overlay was drawn from. reliability: a reliability map that set the opacity, length or threshold of orientation lines.

status.description: unchanged: equal full SHA-256. probable: nothing differs but what was recorded cannot prove the bytes are the same (an equal sampled fingerprint has a blind spot, ADR 0053). changed: the registered file is not what the figure was drawn from (it can be read). changed_on_disk: the file on disk is not what is registered (register it again first). missing: no longer registered, or no readable file.

text.description: The sentence the owner reads about this file

declaration.description: The declarations (unit, orientation interpretation, catalog) in force now against those recorded when the figure was saved. changed and removed are treated like changed data: the owner is asked. not_recorded: the figure was saved before declarations were recorded (not an error). Absent when the dataset is no longer registered.

declarationText.description: The sentence the owner reads about the declarations, e.g. "declaration unchanged" or "declaration changed: unit was K (declared by you), now Jy/beam (declared by you)"

RedrawCheck.description: What "draw again" must tell the owner before it draws. Reads and changes nothing.

kind.description: The description the figure was drawn from; none when it keeps none

state.description: ready: every file is unchanged, draw. ask: say what changed and ask before drawing. blocked: a file cannot be read. none: this figure cannot be drawn again, it is shown as its PNG.

prompt.description: The question or the reason, for ask, blocked and none

masks.description: The masks the figure hatched, when it hatched any; a changed or forgotten one moves the state to ask

ExplorationStep.description: One meaningful state of the viewer (ADR 0057): what was on screen, not its pixels. Mutable working state, pruned oldest first past the cap; not evidence

projectId.description: The open project the step belongs to; 0 when no project was open

parentId.description: The step this one was reached from. Null for the first step of a branch, or when that step was pruned. Several steps with the same parent are branches

datasetId.description: The base dataset of the scene (the owner's id; never sent to a reviewer)

keep.description: How many steps a project keeps

projectId.description: The open project the step belongs to; 0 when no project was open

parentId.description: The step this one was reached from. Null for the first step of a branch, or when that step was pruned. Several steps with the same parent are branches

datasetId.description: The base dataset of the scene (the owner's id; never sent to a reviewer)

scene.description: The scene to restore (scene/1). Only the single-step read and the create reply carry it, and the create reply does not

parentId.description: A step of the same project; continuing from an earlier step makes a branch

BoardExpect.description: What the client last saw at the position it edits (ADR 0057). The edit is applied, in one transaction, only if the panel there is still this one; otherwise nothing changes and the reply is 409 with the current board. Used by undo; a client that omits it gets the unguarded edit.

id.description: The figure's or the job's id

note.description: The panel's note as the client last saw it; omit when the note does not matter

name.description: Unique in the project; what its declarations are labelled with ("declared by your rule <name>"). 1 to 40 letters, digits, blanks, dots, dashes or underscores.

kind.description: glob: a pattern without "/" matches the file name at any depth, one with "/" is anchored at the project folder, "**" stands for any number of folders, matching is case-sensitive. regex: Go (RE2) syntax searched in the relative path.

unit.description: dataset: the unit the files are declared to have. A file that states its own BUNIT keeps it.

angleUnit.description: orientation (required) and catalog angle column: never defaulted.

quantity.description: orientation and catalog angle: b_field, gradient, dust_polarization, starlight_polarization or unspecified; empty means not declared.

coordFormat.description: catalog: degrees, hours_degrees, sexagesimal_hours_degrees or sexagesimal_degrees.

coordFrame.description: catalog: icrs, fk5, fk4 or galactic. Required: the file does not say.

maskType.description: mask (required): what the file flags. Never missing: pixels with no value are computed from the data, not declared.

maskNonzero.description: mask (required): what a nonzero pixel of the file means. Never defaulted.

maskMeaning.description: mask: what the file flags in words; required for type other.

maskTarget.description: mask (required): the project-relative path of the dataset the mask belongs to, with {dir} (the mask's folder, only at the start) and {stem} (its name without extension and without maskStrip), for example {dir}/{stem}.fits.

maskStrip.description: mask: a suffix removed from the mask file's name to get {stem}, for example _mask; the file is left alone when its name lacks it.

ImportRule.description: A researcher import rule (ADR 0058). Which declaration fields a role accepts is checked when the rules are saved.

state.description: none: project.toml holds no rules; same: it holds the saved rules; differs: it holds others; foreign: it holds [[import.rules]] Vesqira did not write, which it never rewrites.

matched.description: Files a rule selects for registration (dataset, orientation or catalog) in the last scan.

pending.description: Of those, files not applied yet at their current size and time.

new.description: Of the pending ones, files the previous scan did not know: "N new files match your rules". Never registered by a scan.

ImportRulesRequest.description: The whole ordered list; the first matching rule wins.

write.description: Must be true: the rules are written to .vesqira/project.toml only on this confirmation.

folder.description: A folder inside the project, relative to it; empty for the whole project.

rescan.description: Walk again; otherwise the last walk (at most ten minutes old) is matched again.

rules.description: A draft list to preview; when absent the saved rules are used. Nothing is saved.

expand.description: A group key (role|extension|author) whose files are all listed (up to 500).

role.description: The built-in role: dataset, catalog, run_record, vgt_psi, vgt_reliability, vgt_support, vgt_fit_rbar2, run_output, rohsa_fit, rohsa_product, config, job_template, archive, other_discipline, declared_data or other.

why.description: The built-in rule behind the role.

proposedRole.description: The built-in role, or the winning rule's role.

by.description: "built-in" or the name of the rule that won.

matched.description: Every rule that matched, in order.

declares.description: What the winning rule would declare, each statement labelled "declared by your rule <name>".

differ.description: The rules would not say the same thing.

truncated.description: The walk stopped at its entry, time or depth budget; what is listed is what was reached.

othersTruncated.description: More unrecognised files exist than the 50 000 that are listed.

ImportPreview.description: What a folder holds under the built-in rules and a list of rules. Read-only: it registers nothing and writes nothing.

confirm.description: Must be true: files are registered only on this confirmation.

paths.description: Only these files (each must be selected by a saved rule); default: every selected file not settled at its current size and time. At most 200 are handled per request; the rest is reported as remaining.

asNew.description: Register these files although a dataset already holds the same bytes (ADR 0053).

outcome.description: declared: already registered, only the rule's declarations applied. duplicate: offered, not registered. skipped: nothing changed, the detail says why.

declared.description: Each declaration applied, labelled "declared by your rule <name>".

matches.description: duplicate: the datasets that already hold the same bytes.

budget.description: tasks of this class that may run at once (--workers-interactive, --workers-heavy, --workers-background)

state.description: unknown: finished, never queued, or not a request of the scientific workers

reason.description: present while waiting: what holds the class's slots, and that interactive viewing is unaffected (heavy and background classes)

Workload.description: Workload classes (ADR 0056). Names only operations, never files or datasets.

text.description: the whole file, plain text, as it is in the zip

SupportPreview.description: A support bundle built and kept in memory for ten minutes; GET /api/support/bundle/{id} returns exactly these files.

includeDatasetNames.description: default false: dataset names and file names are removed from every file

RegionMaskApplied.description: One mask a region spectrum or histogram applied (ADR 0055): what it was, the policy, and how many pixels (summed over the channels read) it flagged with a value and left out. Never a path.

RegionHistogram.description: Counts of the finite values of one channel inside a region, in equal bins from min to max (the largest value falls in the last bin). `no_value` pixels (NaN, BLANK, infinite) are counted apart and before any mask; `excluded_by_mask` counts pixels with a value that a mask left out. Zero is a value. The browser asks for this only when masks are named; the unmasked histogram is counted there.

pixels.description: Pixels of the region inside the image

BoardRect.description: A panel's place on the board's 12-column grid (ADR 0060): column x (0-based) and row y, spanning w columns and h rows. Rows have one fixed height, so y and h count rows.

BoardLayoutRequest.description: The places of every panel of a board, in position order (ADR 0060). A null place clears that panel's. Places must be inside the grid and must not overlap; the server does not compact. expect names the panel at each position and must cover the whole board; from, when present, is the layout being replaced. A mismatch of either is a 409 and nothing changes.

CorrectionEntry.description: One corrected value (ADR 0061): what is in force, what the file says, and the researcher's reason.

value.description: A number or text (the unit, CTYPE, CUNIT, SPECSYS, RADESYS)

file.description: What the file says; null when it has no such card

CorrectionState.description: Every correction in force: the brightness unit (only for a file that states one) and WCS keywords.

wcs.description: By keyword: CRVALi, CRPIXi, CDELTi, CDi_j, PCi_j, CTYPEi, CUNITi, RESTFRQ, RESTFREQ, SPECSYS, EQUINOX, RADESYS

Corrections.description: The researcher's WCS and unit corrections in force on a dataset, from the latest record of their history (ADR 0061). The file and the header facts are never changed. Stale: made for other bytes than the file has now, so applied nowhere until confirmed.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the values (not the reasons)

CorrectionChange.description: What a record changed for one keyword (BUNIT for the unit). null after: not corrected, the file's value applies.

file.description: A number or text (the unit, CTYPE, CUNIT, SPECSYS, RADESYS)

before.description: A number or text (the unit, CTYPE, CUNIT, SPECSYS, RADESYS)

after.description: A number or text (the unit, CTYPE, CUNIT, SPECSYS, RADESYS)

CorrectionRecord.description: One append-only record of the corrections history. A revert is a new record; nothing is edited or deleted.

sizeBytes.description: The registered size of the file it was made for

sourceIdentity.description: sha256:<hex>, sampled:<fingerprint>, or empty when none was recorded

stale.description: Made for other bytes than the file has now

last.description: The latest record id (0 for none): send it back as expect

unitCorrectable.description: The file states a BUNIT and is not an orientation or reliability map

unit.description: Absent: unchanged; null: withdraw the unit correction; text: the corrected unit

wcs.description: Keyword: a value, or null to withdraw that keyword's correction

reason.description: Required, 3 to 500 characters of plain text

reverts.description: For revert: the record to undo (the state goes back to what it was before it)

expect.description: Required to save: the latest record id the client looked at (0 for none); a different one is 409

CorrectionCoords.description: World coordinates by astropy at the image centre and corners, and of the first, middle and last channel.

CorrectionWorkerPreview.description: The worker's validation of a proposed state, as it would be applied; refused carries astropy's or the axis check's reason.

file.description: A number or text (the unit, CTYPE, CUNIT, SPECSYS, RADESYS)

before.description: A number or text (the unit, CTYPE, CUNIT, SPECSYS, RADESYS)

after.description: A number or text (the unit, CTYPE, CUNIT, SPECSYS, RADESYS)

effect.description: live: read again with the new values; pinned: keeps the values it was made with

CorrectionImpact.description: What depends on the dataset's coordinates or unit. Pinned evidence is never changed.

sidecar.description: A vesqira-corrections version 1 document, as exported

confirm.description: Required to apply: the researcher looked at the preview

differentFile.description: Required to apply to a file the sidecar was not made for: why it applies, 10 to 500 characters

madeFor.description: The file name in the sidecar

applies.description: Made for this file (verified or probable): it can be applied without a sentence

CorrectionSidecar.description: The sidecar file (docs/adr/0061): the corrections of one FITS file with the identity of the file they were made for (no path, no catalog id) and their history.

FigureCorrection.description: A correction the figure was drawn under, as the reviewer sees it: no id, no path.

file.description: A number or text (the unit, CTYPE, CUNIT, SPECSYS, RADESYS)

value.description: A number or text (the unit, CTYPE, CUNIT, SPECSYS, RADESYS)

OfflineMark.description: Present on every answer served from the offline store (ADR 0059), as the `offline` field of the JSON head and, serialised, in the X-Vesqira-Offline response header. It says the answer is a copy, when the copy was taken and the file signature it was taken from. A live answer never has it.

identity.description: sha256:… or sampled:… when a content identity was recorded (ADR 0053); empty otherwise

OfflineRequest.description: What to prepare: datasets, or a board (its figures and the datasets they were drawn from), a channel range and how much detail to keep for each plane.

channels.description: Inclusive channel range, clamped to each cube. Absent keeps only the view, the header and the spectra of saved regions.

detail.description: preview keeps the reduced plane the viewer shows first; full also keeps full-resolution planes. An orientation map is only ever kept whole.

budgetBytes.description: The most this preparation may keep. 0 takes the default (256 MiB, or what the store has room for).

status.description: offline: works offline; partial: works partially; remote: needs the remote

reason.description: What is kept and what still needs the host, in words

stale.description: a live look found the file different from the one the copy was made from: kept, never served

MaskSourceRef.description: A dataset, by id and name

Compass.description: Where north (increasing latitude) and east (increasing longitude) of the file's own celestial frame point in the pixel grid at the centre of the map, from the file's WCS with the researcher's corrections applied, if any (projection, CD/PC matrix, flips). Directions are counter-clockwise from +x with y up (FITS), in [0, 360). Never assumes north is up. When available is false there is no celestial WCS to read them from and reason says why: nothing is drawn.

reason.description: Why there is no compass (only when available is false)

x.description: 0-based pixel x of the map centre

y.description: 0-based pixel y of the map centre

frame.description: The astropy name of the celestial frame, when it can be named

corrected.description: The celestial WCS keywords the researcher corrected (ADR 0061) that the arrows rest on; absent when the file's own WCS is used

SubsetBox.description: A rectangle of the source image in whole 0-based pixels, inclusive (the frame regions use).

SubsetChannels.description: A channel range of the source, 0-based and inclusive.

SubsetWorld.description: A spectral interval in world units, resolved to channels by the worker against the WCS in force (ADR 0063): a channel is in when its centre lies in the closed interval. The unit must convert to the axis unit without a convention, and a frame must be the one the file declares.

frame.description: Empty or absent: the file's own

SubsetRegionRef.description: The saved region a box was taken from (a copy of its bounding box).

SubsetDefinition.description: What a subset is: a window onto its source. Absent box or spectral interval mean the whole axis; step keeps every step-th pixel of the box (values untouched).

SubsetView.description: A virtual subset (ADR 0063): never a file. Stale: the source file is no longer the one this version was pinned to, so it is read nowhere until re-pinned.

identity.description: sha256:… or sampled:…, empty when none was recorded

materialised.description: The dataset written from this version for the source as it is now, when one exists and is unchanged

SubsetVersion.description: One row of the append-only history.

SubsetMade.description: A dataset written from a version of the subset.

SubsetInput.description: Create or edit a subset. The box is given directly or taken from a saved region of the source (regionId: its bounding box, clipped to the image), not both. The worker checks every bound against the real file.

reason.description: Required, up to 500 characters of plain text

expectVersion.description: Edit: the version the person was looking at; a newer one is a 409

carryMasks.description: The masks of the source to carry into the file, cut by the subset's window (a mask not listed is left behind; the no-value mask is computed again from the file, never carried). A request with another choice is another file: a file is reused only for the same choice.

SubsetWindow.description: What the window resolved to, in the source file's own 0-based pixels and channels, echoed by the worker in every reply that read through it. A reply without it is refused.

channel_rule.description: The rule that chose the channels

geometry.description: The worker's view of the window: size, channels, window, sky and spectral facts

SubsetMaterialised.description: The file written from a version of a subset, an ordinary dataset with a derived record naming the subset, its version and the source identity. reused: the same subset, version and source bytes (with the same corrections and declared unit) had already been written and the file is unchanged.

RunViewSpec.description: What a saved view of the runs table remembers: words and keys only, never a run id or a value.

query.description: The filter words, as typed in the filter box

columns.description: Exposed columns: a fixed one (status, host, generated, imported, qc, kind), p:<parameter> or m:<result>

y.description: A result key; empty when none is chosen

by.description: A parameter key to colour by; empty for none

name.description: One line; saving under an existing name (any case) replaces that view

SceneMask.description: A typed mask hatched over the plane of a saved figure (ADR 0055), by what it was when it was drawn. The server fills type, name, tier and fingerprint from its own row and refuses a mask of another dataset, a stale one, or a fingerprint that is not the row's.

RedrawMask.description: A mask the figure hatched, compared with the catalog now (ADR 0055). No id and no path.

status.description: changed: another fingerprint, made from other bytes than the dataset has now, or its file changed. forgotten: no longer in the catalog. Either is announced before drawing, and its hatch is left out of the new drawing.

CarryChoice.description: What to do with one mask of the source in the file an operation writes (ADR 0055): carry it (cut or resampled with the data, a new mask of the result with its own rule and fingerprint) or leave it behind (recorded). Nothing is carried unless asked; align and convolve want every mask decided.

ConvertRunValuesRequest.description: Numbers a run declared, with the unit each was recorded in, to be expressed in one target unit (cross-run plot, ADR 0062). Up to 5000 values; give `to` and `values`. No dataset is involved. Alternatively give only `pairs` for a dry run: which (from, to) pairs would convert, answered without any value (up to 200; `to` and `values` must then be absent).

to.description: The target unit, as the primary panel records it.

uncertainty.description: Absent or null when the run states none: not zero.

pairs.description: Dry run. One answer per pair, in order; a refusal of one pair does not hide the others.

to.description: The unit to convert it to.

ConvertRunValuesResponse.description: Plain dimensional conversion by astropy.units with no equivalency (no beam, frame, rest frequency or spectral axis is assumed). When refused is true nothing is converted and reason says why; otherwise results holds one entry per request value, in order. For a dry run (`pairs` in the request), refused is false and pairs holds the answer for each pair; no numbers are converted.

from.description: The recorded unit that could not be converted.

to.description: The target unit in astropy's spelling.

factors.description: The multiplier from each recorded unit to the target.

reason.description: In words, why this pair is not converted; present when refused.

factor.description: The multiplier from the recorded unit to the target; present when not refused.

CrossRunConversion.description: What was converted into the target unit of a cross-run plot: plain unit conversion by the worker, no equivalency.

FigureRunPlot.description: Reviewer-safe account of a cross-run plot: the filter words, the axes, how many runs and the conversion. It has no run id, name or value.

CrossRunDescription.description: cross-run/1: the owner-only description a cross-run plot was drawn from, written by the server from its own reading of the runs (ADR 0065). It names run ids, names and recorded values, so it is never copied into a snapshot, a report or a review.

y.description: What the run recorded; never replaced by a conversion.

converted.description: The number the plot drew, when the run was converted.

CreateRunFigureRequest.description: Saves a cross-run plot as a figure (ADR 0065). The server reads the runs itself; the browser says which runs, which axes and which conversion. A conversion is accepted only when the worker, asked again, gives the factor the browser used.

redrawnFrom.description: The cross-run plot this one redraws

SceneCompass.description: The north and east arrows a saved figure drew (ADR 0047, amendment) and the WCS state they rest on, as the worker read it for the viewer (Compass). The arrows stand at pixel (x, y) of the figure's plane: 0-based pixel-centre coordinates, y up. Absent when the figure drew none (the option was off, or the file has no celestial WCS) and from figures saved before it existed, which draw again exactly as before. The server keeps what the browser reported and cannot read the WCS again; the reviewer's provenance says so.

northDeg.description: Counter-clockwise from +x with y up (FITS), in [0, 360)

eastDeg.description: Counter-clockwise from +x with y up (FITS), in [0, 360)

frame.description: The astropy name of the celestial frame, when it could be named

corrected.description: The celestial WCS keywords the researcher corrected (ADR 0061) that the arrows rest on; absent when the file's own WCS is used

Account.description: A group-server account (ADR 0050 section 2). It carries no credential.

username.description: the sub of its local (password) identity

AuthState.description: Where this browser is in signing in. second_factor and enrol are the pending stages after a correct password.

setupNeeded.description: no admin exists yet: run `vesqira-api admin bootstrap` on the server

recent.description: signed in within the recent sign-in window

SecondFactorRequest.description: A six-digit TOTP code, or one recovery code.

Enrolment.description: A pending TOTP enrolment: the secret in base32 and its otpauth:// URI (SHA1, 6 digits, 30 s).

RecoveryCodes.description: Ten single-use recovery codes, shown once; only their hashes are kept.

AccessToken.description: A personal access token, without its value (which is never kept).

workspace.description: The one workspace a push or relay token acts in (ADR 0066); absent for an account-wide token.

scopes.description: write includes read; push sends frozen work and relay takes run requests for a linked computer (ADR 0066), both bound to the current workspace

token.description: the value, shown in this answer only

SignedOutEverywhere.description: Every session of the account ended. Access tokens are not sessions and stay valid.

VgtHeader.description: The VGT.jl keywords of a product header as the file states them, mapped onto Vesqira's orientation declaration by one reading (mapping version 1). Everything here is declared by the file and none of it is verified.

product.description: VGTPROD: the product's role (psi, reliability, fit_rbar2, support).

psiFrame.description: PSIFRAME as written. Absent in older VGT output; its absence is never inferred from the WCS.

params.description: The VGT* run parameters and the input beam (INB*), for a file imported without a run_metadata.toml. Values that name a place on a machine are dropped.

resolution.description: The worker's reading of the keywords' resolution. status is approximate (the input beam and the smoothing Gaussian in quadrature, in arcseconds; the dn window is a top-hat and is not included) or not_established, with reasons. Declared and approximate, never verified; unlike a beam it is not read from BMAJ.

orientation.description: The declaration the header makes; null when PSIFRAME is absent or unknown (nothing is inferred).

basis.description: Per field: file (the header states it) or convention (only the unit, when BUNIT does not state rad or deg).

notes.description: Why part of the header was not used (an unknown PSIFRAME or PSIANGLE, a BUNIT that is not an angle unit).

conflicts.description: Where the declaration in force differs from the header, in full sentences. The declaration in force stays in use; nothing is resolved silently.

quotaBytes.description: bytes of managed copies and derived outputs it may keep

Workspace.description: A workspace: the access unit of the group server (ADR 0050 slice 3).

Membership.description: An account's role in one workspace.

Invitation.description: An invitation waiting to be accepted; its secret is never shown again.

link.description: shown once; the secret is in the URL fragment

invitations.description: empty unless the caller may invite

roots.description: the data folders declared for the workspace

MemberComment.description: A comment by a signed-in member on a figure or a report of the workspace.

permissions.description: the caller's effective permissions here (x-vesqira-permission names); the server still enforces every one

WorkspaceContext.description: Where the request acts and what the caller may do there. Group server only.

HealpixHeader.description: What the worker read from a HEALPix map's table header when it was registered (ADR 0067). A map that does not state POLCCONV and COORDSYS is refused at registration, so both are always present. The pixels stay in the file.

coordsys.description: COORDSYS as the file writes it (G, GALACTIC, C, E, ...)

frame.description: The system COORDSYS names; only galactic maps are sampled in this version

polcconv.description: The polarization convention: COSMO maps have U of the opposite sign to IAU

stokes_unit.description: TUNIT of Q_STOKES as written (for example K_CMB); never converted

has_qu_cov.description: False: the Q-U covariance is taken as 0 when sigma_P is computed, and the result says so

datasetId.description: A HEALPix map (kind healpix) on this computer

targetId.description: The dataset on this computer whose celestial grid receives the map

product.description: dust_polarization: psi = 1/2 atan2(U, Q); b_field: psi + 90 degrees

method.description: How Q and U are sampled; nearest when left out

fwhmArcmin.description: The Gaussian's FWHM on the sphere, for method gaussian only; at least the map's pixel size, at most 600

snrMin.description: Blank the angle where P/sigma_P is below this; P and sigma_P are kept everywhere

HealpixSampleSummary.description: What the worker did: the parameters, how the result was derived (convention, frame rotation, sampling, smoothing, noise), the counts, the P/sigma_P filter and a policy sentence for a reviewer

dataset.description: The angle map, declared by the operation (axial, degrees, sky frame of the grid, the product as quantity)

p.description: The companion P map; null if it could not be registered

sigmaP.description: The companion sigma_P map; null if it could not be registered

RerunInputIdentity.description: What the catalog knew about the chosen input cube when the draft was made (ADR 0053). sampledFp is sampled/1, which is not a hash of the whole file; fullSha256 is the SHA-256 of every byte. Either is empty when none was computed; neither is computed for a draft.
